summary: Eva Wilden is an Indologist who completed her MA, Promotion, and Habilitation at the University of Hamburg between ~1985 and ~2004, studying under Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan. She held posts at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (2003) and Hamburg (2017).

Evald Lidén was an indologist and linguist who earned his M.A. from Uppsala University (1883–1895). He served as PD of Indo-European linguistics at Uppsala (1895), acting professor of comparative linguistics and Sanskrit (1899), and head at Gothenburg (1917–1929).

Evan Thompson is a philosopher who studied at Amherst College and the University of Toronto (Ph.D. 1990) under Robert A. F. Thurman and Francisco Varela. His main posts include Concordia, York, Toronto (2005–2013), and British Columbia (2013).
Eveline Masilamani-Meyer is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who earned her Ph.D. at Heidelberg University under the supervision of Ayyadurai Dhamotharan.
Evelyn Frederick Charles Ludowyk was a scholar in history and archaeology who studied at Richmond College. He served as Professor of English at the University of Ceylon from ~1942 to 1956.
Evert Willem Beth was a philosopher who studied at Utrecht University (~1925–1935). He held a post at Johns Hopkins University in ~1952 and served at the University of Amsterdam from 1946 until 1964.

Evgenij Mihajlovič Medvedev was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology who studied at Moscow State University (~1951–1956). He worked at the Institute of Oriental Studies (1956–1957) and served as Director at Moscow State University in 1960.

Eviatar Shulman is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed his BA at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (1998–2009), where he was appointed Associate Professor and Department Chair in 2009.

Eyal Aviv is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and philosophy. He earned his Ph.D. at Harvard University under Robert M. Gimello, Parimal G. Patil, and Michael Puett, and held a post at George Washington University in 2014.

F. B. J. Kuiper was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Leiden and Utrecht under Uhlenbeck, Caland, van Wijk, and Vogel. He taught classics at Carpentier Alting Stichting (1934–1939) and was a professor at Leiden (1939–1972).
F. Garritsen was an Indology scholar who studied at Utrecht University under the instruction of Jan Gonda.

F. Gelpke worked in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Rostock and Göttingen under Emil Sieg, Jacob Wackernagel, and Hermann Oldenberg, and served as an assistant at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin in 1932.

F. J. Richards was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at Exeter College (1893–1902). He served as a lecturer and honorary lecturer in Indian archaeology at SOAS University of London in 1934 and 1939.

F. M. G. Lorimer worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and history. After studying at Somerville College (1902–1905), she held library posts at the Bodleian (1907–1909), the Royal Asiatic Society (1932–1940), and the Royal Horticultural Society.
Fa Qing is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate from the University of Calgary (attested 2001), where he studied under Leslie S. Kawamura, Anthony W. Barber, and Xiaojie Yang.
Fa Yao is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under K. L. Dhammajoti and was attested as a Visiting Lecturer of Theravada Buddhism at the University of Chicago in 2026.

Fabian Wilhelm af Ekenstam was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned his doctorate at Lund University (1805–1808). He held theology posts at Lund (1809, 1812) and taught philosophy at Katedralskolan, Linköping (1822–1837).

Fabienne Jagou is a scholar of Tibetology and history who completed her PhD at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences (~1993–1999) under Pierre-Étienne Will. She became Maître de conférences at the EFEO in ~2001.

Fabio Rambelli specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Ca' Foscari, Naples "L'Orientale", and Tokyo, under Massimo Raveri and Adriana Boscaro. He held posts at Sapporo University (2001–2002) and UC Santa Barbara (~2010).

Fabrizia Baldissera is an Indologist who studied at the Department of Mathematics "Federigo Enriques" (1969–2004) and held posts at the University of Florence (attested 1999) and the University of Naples "L'Orientale".
